newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks extend gains in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks extend gains in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices extended early gains in late Thursday trade as financials emerged to lead stocks upward, brokers said.
With 55 minutes left in trade, the index was up 58.29 points or 0.68 percent at 8,635.23. Turnover was a brisk T$98 billion.
Financials, which lagged recent gains, rose 2.2 percent, with the "Big Three" state-run banks surging due to a government privatisation programme, brokers said.
Chang Hwa Bank rose T$4.5 to T$120, First Commercial gained T$4 to T$120 and Hua Nan Bank surged T$5.5 to T$116.5.
"Most analysts estimate the future underwriting price of the Big Three would be around T$130 each, so their prices have potential to rise," said Capital Securities manager Alex Chiu.
Steel and paper shares rose, but foods, plastics and constructions fell.
Brokers noted heavy resistance around 8,650-8,700 points.
"The index should consolidate in coming sessions within a 8,450-8,750 range, but performance by each share or sector will vary largely," Chiu said.
